fact_check.claim: 'Can Kaspa realistically reach a dollar this cycle? Yeah, I think so, maybe we got a few more years to prove it' (transcript, answering chat)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own forward-looking prediction, written in first person. The supporting numbers are verified on 2026-09-30: $KAS $0.0440, market cap about $1.22B, rank 71, +15.2% 7d, +57.5% 30d, 78.8% below its ATH of $0.2074 (2024-07-31); circulating supply 27.73B of a 28.70B max (96.6%, written 'about 97%'); $1 x 27.73B = about $27.7B; $1 / $0.044 = about 22.7x, written 'roughly 23x'. Used in the Kaspa tweet, the engagement-bait one-liner, YT post 2, thread 2, both polls and both IG captions.

fact_check.claim: Zcash: 'just another token', miners like it, 'I don't know if there's any point of Zcash in the long run', 'if they wanted to turn Kaspa into an optional privacy network they could do it, I saw a project like that for Kaspa', 'not like I'm going to be DCAing into Zcash'; 'you can mine both Kaspa and Zcash at the same time' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's opinion, written as his view ('in my view a feature like that can be built on top of Kaspa'); the unnamed Kaspa privacy project is NOT named (unverified). Zcash numbers verified 2026-09-30: $ZEC $1,412.65, market cap about $23.97B, rank 9 to 10 on CoinGecko (written 'top 10', 'about $24B'), +65.6% 30d (written 'about 66% on the month'). The 'mine Kaspa and Zcash at the same time' line could NOT be verified (different hash algorithms) and is dropped, as is 'even though it's a DAG'.
fact_check.source: api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/markets?ids=zcash and top-12 by market cap (2026-09-30); transcript

fact_check.claim: Kaspa context used in YT post 2 / thread 2: 10 blocks per second, fair launch with no premine, the first vProg live on testnet; Mike's vProgs video pulled 3,600 views in one day (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: 10 BPS since the Crescendo hard fork (May 2025) and the fair launch are established public facts (persona core_theses). The first vProg (a verifiable tic-tac-toe game, real off-chain execution with ZK settlement on the L1) on testnet was verified in the beer-and-kaspa plan (KuCoin news 2026-09-27, github.com/biryukovmaxim/vprog-tictactoe); written 'went live on testnet in September', testnet only. The 3,600 views figure is Mike's own channel stat stated on stream, used once in the YT post as his statement.

fact_check.claim: 'Unbelievably good economic news': ADP employment change better than expected and more than double prior; PCE month over month and year over year better than expected; GDP quarter over quarter final better than expected and better than prior; personal spending better than expected; corporate profits negative (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified for Sept 30, 2026 and numbers added: ADP +90K vs 73K forecast, prior 38K (more than double, as Mike said); headline PCE (August) 0.3% m/m vs 0.4% forecast and 3.4% y/y vs 3.7% forecast; core PCE under forecast on both readings (sources disagree on the core y/y figure, 3.0% vs 3.3%, so NO core number is written, only 'core came in under forecast too'); Q2 GDP final 2.2% annualized vs 1.5% forecast (the prior estimate is reported inconsistently, so 'better than prior' is not written). Personal spending and corporate profits could not be pinned to a figure and are not used. Stocks rose on the day (Nasdaq about +1%).
fact_check.source: investing.com/news/stock-market-news/adp-jobs-data-gdp-core-pce-and-oil-inventories-due-wednesday-93CH-4923296 (forecasts and priors); foxbusiness.com/economy/august-2026-pce-inflation (2026-09-30); mediacenter.adp.com (August +38K); WebSearch summary of the Sept 30 releases (ADP 90K, GDP 2.2%)

fact_check.claim: 'There was supposed to be another rate hike on October 28; the probability of a rate pause increased to 62% compared to 50' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: CME FedWatch showed a 65.1% probability of a hold on Oct 28 vs 34.9% for a 25 bp hike after the data, 'essentially an even split the previous day' (Fox Business, Sept 30); prediction markets 65% hold / 34% hike the same evening (DeFiRate); one week earlier FedWatch priced a 70.9% chance of a hike (CoinEdition). Copy: 'about 65% odds of no hike, from a coin flip the day before; a week ago about a 70% chance of a hike'. Mike's on-stream 62% is replaced by the updated 65%. Kevin Warsh as Fed chair is confirmed by the same coverage but he is not named in copy.

fact_check.claim: Bitcoin: the previous resistance (the May high) is now acting as support and the daily candles keep bouncing off it; Benjamin Cowen is 'perplexed' that Bitcoin went above the May high; Bitcoin dominance is falling off a cliff and 'others excluding top 10' is on the rise; people are buying back in because the bottom is in (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: $BTC $83,444 on 2026-09-30, daily closes between $83.4K and $86.6K every day since Sept 22, above the May 2026 peak near $82,000 (level not quoted as a number in copy; written 'so far it will not go below'). Bitcoin dominance 58.3% (CoinGecko global), below 60% since the week ending Sept 26 (Yahoo Finance). Cowen: his own X post 'Bitcoin broke through the May high this week, which I clearly got wrong' (verified in the spon plan) and BeInCrypto/Mitrade 'Waited for Bitcoin's October Bottom? Benjamin Cowen Says He Was Wrong'; copy quotes only 'clearly got wrong', the word 'perplexed' is NOT used. 'Everything outside the top 10 is climbing' is Mike's chart read, written as his read. October seasonality added from CoinEdition: Bitcoin closed October higher in 10 of 15 years (2011 to 2025).
fact_check.source: api.coingecko.com (bitcoin market_chart 21d, /global, 2026-09-30); finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-share-crypto-market-drops-170914034.html; mitrade.com/au/insights/crypto/bitcoin/beincrypto-BTCUSD-202609220948; repurpose/output/spon-lane3-plan.json fact_check; coinedition.com (October seasonality)

fact_check.verdict: Mike's own thesis, written in first person and per persona core_theses: the zombies all planned to buy an October bottom, so their own demand turns October green and the real low prints before October; never written as the zombies causing a bottom in October.

yt_posts.body_style: stat-stack arc: the three beats and the Fed odds in the pre-fold hook, the numbered data, what it did to the Oct 28 odds, the everything-plus-crypto scenario, the Bitcoin chart and the Cowen tell, the zombie mechanics and October seasonality, a forked price question and a like/subscribe ask
yt_posts.body:
Jobs beat. Inflation cooled. GDP got revised up. All on the same day, and the odds of a Fed rate hike on Oct 28 fell off a cliff.

Here is why I told my group I do not know if we could ask for anything better, and what it sets up for October.

The data, all from Sept 30:

1. Jobs. ADP private payrolls came in at +90K against 73K expected, more than double the prior month's 38K.

2. Inflation. PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, printed 3.4% year over year against 3.7% expected, and 0.3% on the month against 0.4%. Core came in under forecast too. One more reading that says inflation is cooling.

3. Growth. The final read on Q2 GDP came in at 2.2% against 1.5% expected.

Employment, inflation, GDP: every one of them better than expected on the same day.

What it did to the Fed. A week ago the market was pricing about a 70% chance of another rate hike on Oct 28. After this data, the odds of NO hike jumped to about 65%, from a coin flip the day before. We need more readings like this and we will be absolutely flying.

Now put crypto on top of that. For the past year every other market did well while crypto sat in a bear market. The scenario I like even more than crypto running alone is everything doing well AND crypto doing well, because that means more money flows into crypto.

And the chart agrees. Bitcoin ($BTC) broke above its May high, and that old resistance is now acting as support: it keeps tapping it on the daily candles and so far it will not go below. Bitcoin dominance is under 60% while the chart of everything outside the top 10 keeps climbing. Benjamin Cowen posted that he 'clearly got wrong' the break above the May high.

That is the part the four-year cycle zombies never see coming. They all planned to buy an October bottom, so their own demand turns October green, and in my read the real low is already behind us. For what it is worth, Bitcoin has closed October higher in 10 of the last 15 years.

So bet right now, in the comments: does Bitcoin close October above $90K, or does the Fed spoil the party on Oct 28?

Click that like button and click the subscribe button if you want the macro read that ignores the four-year cycle echo chamber.

yt_posts.body:
Can Kaspa realistically reach $1 this cycle? Somebody asked me that on stream this week and my answer is yes. Maybe it takes a few more years to prove it, but yes.

Here is the math that makes $1 a lot less crazy than it sounds, and the coin that proves the market will pay for it.

Where we are. Kaspa ($KAS) trades around 4.4 cents, about a $1.2B market cap. It is up about 15% on the week and about 57% on the month, and it is still about 79% under its all-time high of 20.7 cents from July 2024.

The math. There are about 27.7 billion $KAS in circulation out of a 28.7 billion max, so about 97% of the supply is already out. No premine, no VC unlocks waiting to get dumped on you. At $1, that is a market cap of about $27.7B, roughly 23x from here.

Now the comp. Zcash ($ZEC) is sitting in the top 10 this week at about a $24B market cap, up about 66% on the month. Somebody asked me what I think about Zcash. It is another proof-of-work coin you can make money on, but I am not DCAing into it. Optional privacy is a feature, and in my view a feature like that can be built on top of Kaspa.

But look at what that number tells you. The market is paying about $24B for a proof-of-work coin RIGHT NOW. Kaspa at $1 is a $27.7B coin. We are not talking about some fantasy valuation; we are talking about a market cap the market is already handing to a PoW coin this week.

And Kaspa is not standing still. It runs 10 blocks per second on proof of work. The first vProg (a verifiable program: real off-chain execution with zero-knowledge settlement on the L1) went live on testnet in September. I put out a video on vProgs and it pulled 3,600 views in a single day, so people are paying attention.

Fair launch, almost fully mined, 10 blocks per second, and programmability on the way. That is why I say $1.

So tell me in the comments: does $KAS hit $1 this cycle, does it take a few more years, or does it never get there?

Click that like button and click the subscribe button if you want to be early on the next Kaspa move.
